### Case Summary ###
**Clinical Impression:**  
Highly suspicious for **resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma of the head**, based on:  
- Clinical presentation: Painless obstructive jaundice (elevated direct bilirubin), unintentional weight loss (>5% over 1 month), fatigue, and possible subtle acholia (unreported but not denied)  
- Biochemical profile: Mixed hepatocellular-cholestatic LFT pattern with predominant cholestasis (↑ ALP, ↑ GGT, ↑ total & direct bilirubin; ALT/AST only mildly elevated); preserved synthetic function (normal albumin, INR)  
- Imaging triad:  
  • Distal common bile duct and main pancreatic duct stricture with upstream dilation (“double duct sign”) on MRCP and CT  
  • Hypodense, irregular 2.7 cm pancreatic head mass on contrast-enhanced CT  
  • Hypoechoic, heterogeneous, abutting (non-encasing) mass on EUS with successful FNA  
- Exclusion of mimics:  
  • No biliary stones (US, MRCP)  
  • Normal serum IgG4 (58 mg/dL; rules out IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis/pancreatitis)  
  • No imaging features of PSC or primary liver malignancy  

**Pending:**  
- EUS-FNA cytology/histopathology (critical for diagnosis)  
- Serum CA 19-9 (not yet provided — important for baseline, prognosis, and monitoring)  

**Next Steps Recommended:**  
1. Expedite pathology review of FNA specimen (consider cell block, immunohistochemistry if indeterminate)  
2. Obtain serum CA 19-9  
3. Multidisciplinary tumor board referral for resectability assessment (CT already suggests no distant metastases or local vascular invasion — portal vein abutment without encasement is generally considered borderline resectable)  
4. Nutritional assessment and biliary decompression planning (e.g., ERCP ± stent) if jaundice worsens or pruritus/cholestasis complications arise  

No evidence supports benign or inflammatory etiology at this time. Malignancy is the leading diagnosis.

Diagnostician:

[THOUGHT]  
The clinical summary presents a classic presentation of resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) of the head. The triad of painless obstructive jaundice, weight loss, and fatigue — in the absence of biliary stones or IgG4-related disease — strongly favors malignancy. Biochemically, the cholestasis-predominant LFT pattern with preserved synthetic function aligns with extrahepatic biliary obstruction rather than primary hepatocellular disease. Imaging findings are highly specific: the “double duct sign” (simultaneous dilation of CBD and MPD due to a distal obstruction), a hypodense, irregular, 2.7 cm mass in the pancreatic head on contrast-enhanced CT, and corroborating EUS features (hypoechoic, heterogeneous, abutting but not encasing vessels) collectively meet radiologic criteria for PDAC. Critically, benign mimics have been actively excluded: no stones on US/MRCP, normal IgG4 level (58 mg/dL; well below diagnostic threshold of >135 mg/dL for IgG4-RD), and no imaging signs of PSC or metastatic liver disease. While EUS-FNA cytology and CA 19-9 remain pending, the pretest probability is extremely high — these tests are confirmatory, not diagnostic gatekeepers, in this context. The tumor board referral and resectability assessment are appropriate next steps, but do not alter the most likely diagnosis. No other entity explains the full constellation: autoimmune pancreatitis would show elevated IgG4 and often diffuse gland enlargement; chronic pancreatitis would show calcifications, ductal irregularity, or atrophy — none reported; ampullary carcinoma may mimic but typically presents with earlier bleeding or less pronounced ductal dilation; cholangiocarcinoma would originate in the bile duct, not the pancreatic head parenchyma, and rarely causes such symmetric double-duct dilation without intrinsic ductal mass.

- Unintentional weight loss >5% over 1 month  
- Fatigue as a systemic symptom  
- Mixed hepatocellular-cholestatic LFT pattern with predominant cholestasis (↑ ALP, ↑ GGT, ↑ total & direct bilirubin; only mild ALT/AST elevation)  
- Preserved synthetic function (normal albumin, normal INR)  
- “Double duct sign”: distal common bile duct and main pancreatic duct stricture with upstream dilation on MRCP and CT  
- Hypodense, irregular 2.7 cm mass in the pancreatic head on contrast-enhanced CT  
- Hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass on EUS that abuts but does not encase vessels  
- No biliary stones identified on ultrasound or MRCP  
- Normal serum IgG4 level (58 mg/dL), ruling out IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis/pancreatitis  
- No imaging features of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) or primary liver malignancy
